newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand first developing nation to ban CFCs - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Thailand first developing nation to ban CFCs - U.N.

text.p: Thailand has become the first developing nation in the world to ban the production and import of domestic refrigerators with chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), a United Nations environmental agency said on Friday.

The Thai government's ban takes effect on January 1, 1997, only one year after the deadline imposed on developed countries by the U.N.'s Montreal Protocol, said a statement by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

CFCs, which are widely used as coolants in refigerators and air conditioners, are believed to be a major contributor to the destruction of the Earth's protective ozone layer. Less ozone means an increase in damaging ultraviolet radiation from the sun, damaging crops and increasing the risk of skin cancer for humans and animals.
The Montreal Protocol is a phase-out plan for the offending chemicals crafted in 1987 under which developed countries last year stopped production and imports of CFCs.

"The phase-out of Thailand is an important achievement of the Montreal Protocol, and gives testimony to the power of constructive cooperation between developed and developing countries, and between industry and government," said UNEP.
"Actions taken by the Thai government to phase out production and import of CFC refrigerators will serve as a model to other developing countries," it added.
The Thai domestic refrigerator industry has grown rapidly in the past decade with seven companies producing over 1.2 million refrigerators annually for local and export markets.
